phase: Reference Mode Recovery — Sectoral Financial Positions / Phase A strict explicit-instrument gate

missing_address_interpretation.implication: The strict explicit-instrument asset-transaction sum for C cannot be formed.
The strict explicit-instrument liability-transaction sum for G cannot be formed.
The strict explicit-instrument liability stock sum for G cannot be formed.
The strict explicit-instrument liability-transaction sum for H cannot be formed.
The strict explicit-instrument liability stock sum for H cannot be formed.

scientific_interpretation: The boundary review remains conceptually valid: aggregate sector positions are legitimate behaviour-over-time targets distinct from bilateral Accounting Spine completion.

However the preregistered strict materialization rule required every F2-F8 component to be directly published for each required sector/side. Eight exact QSA series are unavailable, so five aggregate addresses cannot be formed without an additional structural/applicability rule or a different exact published aggregate identity.

No unavailable component is converted to zero and no residual is allocated. The absence of a complete strict sum is therefore a valid negative source-coverage result rather than an accounting inconsistency.
Because no complete six-sector series exists under the preregistered strict gate, stock/flow system reconciliation cannot be evaluated and no promotion is allowed.
prohibited_post_result_shortcuts: convert the eight unavailable series to zero because they appear economically small or structurally implausible
drop H, G or C from the required sector boundary after observing source gaps
replace financial transactions with first differences of stocks
use a total-F series without a separately preregistered instrument-boundary treatment
treat the 160 available component series as sufficient for promotion

disposition.next_justified_path: A separately preregistered Phase B may test a direct published aggregate identity only if it preserves the RMD F2-F8 instrument boundary without missing-to-zero assumptions. Phase A values may not be used to tune the Phase B promotion criterion.
